inputs.goal:
You are a Kubernetes workflow orchestrator. Your goal is to run a LAMMPS simulation using a MiniCluster, monitor its execution, and extract a performance metric (FOM) from its logs. Follow these steps precisely:

1. **Deploy the MiniCluster**: Apply the following manifest to the cluster.
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
   kind: MiniCluster
   metadata:
     name: lammps-fom-test
     namespace: default
   spec:
     size: 2
     tasks: 1
     container:
       image: docker.io/vanessa/fractale-test:lammps
       command: lmp -v -log lammps.log -in examples/reaxff/HNS/in.reaxc.hns
       imagePullPolicy: Always
       workingDir: /data
   ```
2. **Monitor the Job**: Wait for the `lammps-fom-test-0` pod to reach the 'Completed' state. You can check the status of the MiniCluster and its pods using `kubectl get minicluster lammps-fom-test` and `kubectl get pods -l flux-framework.org/minicluster-name=lammps-fom-test`.

3. **Handle Failures**: If the pod enters a 'Failed' or 'Error' state, use `kubectl logs lammps-fom-test-0` and `kubectl describe pod lammps-fom-test-0` to investigate the cause. Report the error and stop.

4. **Extract the FOM**: Once the job is complete, retrieve the logs from the `lammps-fom-test-0` pod. Parse the `lammps.log` file within the pod's output to find the 'Total wall time'. This value is the Figure of Merit (FOM).

5. **Report the Result**: Return a JSON object containing the success status and the extracted FOM. For example: `{"success": true, "fom": "<extracted_wall_time>"}`.

6. **Cleanup**: After extracting the logs and FOM, delete the MiniCluster resource using `kubectl delete minicluster lammps-fom-test`.

GROUP:      flux-framework.org
KIND:       MiniCluster
VERSION:    v1alpha2

FIELD: spec <Object>


DESCRIPTION:
    MiniCluster is an HPC cluster in Kubernetes you can control
    Either to submit a single job (and go away) or for a persistent single- or
    multi- user cluster
    
FIELDS:
  archive	<Object>
    Archive to load or save

  backoffLimit	<integer>
    BackoffLimit is the number of retries for the job before failing

  cleanup	<boolean>
    Cleanup the pods and storage when the index broker pod is complete

  containers	<[]Object> -required-
    Containers is one or more containers to be created in a pod.
    There should only be one container to run flux with runFlux

  deadlineSeconds	<integer>
    Should the job be limited to a particular number of seconds?
    Approximately one year. This cannot be zero or job won't start

  flux	<Object>
    Flux options for the broker, shared across cluster

  interactive	<boolean>
    Run a single-user, interactive minicluster

  jobLabels	<map[string]string>
    Labels for the job

  logging	<Object>
    Logging modes determine the output you see in the job log

  maxSize	<integer>
    MaxSize (maximum number of pods to allow scaling to)

  minSize	<integer>
    MinSize (minimum number of pods that must be up for Flux)
    Note that this option does not edit the number of tasks,
    so a job could run with fewer (and then not start)

  network	<Object>
    A spec for exposing or defining the cluster headless service

  pod	<Object>
    Pod spec details

  services	<[]Object>
    Services are one or more service containers to bring up
    alongside the MiniCluster.

  shareProcessNamespace	<boolean>
    Share process namespace?

  size	<integer>
    Size (number of job pods to run, size of minicluster in pods)
    This is also the minimum number required to start Flux

  tasks	<integer>
    Total number of CPUs being run across entire cluster

GROUP:      flux-framework.org
KIND:       MiniCluster
VERSION:    v1alpha2

FIELD: containers <[]Object>


DESCRIPTION:
    Containers is one or more containers to be created in a pod.
    There should only be one container to run flux with runFlux
    
FIELDS:
  batch	<boolean>
    Indicate that the command is a batch job that will be written to a file to
    submit

  batchRaw	<boolean>
    Don't wrap batch commands in flux submit (provide custom logic myself)

  command	<string>
    Single user executable to provide to flux start

  commands	<Object>
    More specific or detailed commands for just workers/broker

  environment	<map[string]string>
    Key/value pairs for the environment

  image	<string>
    Container image must contain flux and flux-sched install

  imagePullPolicy	<string>
    Allow the user to dictate pulling directly

  imagePullSecret	<string>
    Allow the user to pull authenticated images
    By default no secret is selected. Setting
    this with the name of an already existing
    imagePullSecret will specify that secret
    in the pod spec.

  launcher	<boolean>
    Indicate that the command is a launcher that will
    ask for its own jobs (and provided directly to flux start)

  lifeCycle	<Object>
    Lifecycle can handle post start commands, etc.

  logs	<string>
    Log output directory

  name	<string>
    Container name is only required for non flux runners

  noWrapEntrypoint	<boolean>
    Do not wrap the entrypoint to wait for flux, add to path, etc?

  ports	<[]integer>
    Ports to be exposed to other containers in the cluster
    We take a single list of integers and map to the same

  pullAlways	<boolean>
    Allow the user to dictate pulling
    By default we pull if not present. Setting
    this to true will indicate to pull always

  resources	<Object>
    Resources include limits and requests

  runFlux	<boolean>
    Application container intended to run flux (broker)

  secrets	<map[string]Object>
    Secrets that will be added to the environment
    The user is expected to create their own secrets for the operator to find

  securityContext	<Object>
    Security Context
    https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

  volumes	<map[string]Object>
    Existing volumes that can be mounted

  workingDir	<string>
    Working directory to run command from
